primitives.name: Temporal Contact Graph Encoding
primitives.verbatim_quote: Method / model Graph construction: each ball contact is a node; consecutive contacts (pass→set→hit→block) receive directed edges, forming the rally's temporal chain.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'V': 'set of ball contacts (nodes)', 'E': 'set of directed temporal edges between contacts', 't': 'time index of contact', 'c_i': 'contact type (pass/set/hit/block)'}
primitives.assumptions: Each contact is a discrete event with unique time index; edges represent sequential dependency; node features are static per contact.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When contact sequence is incomplete or ambiguous, graph structure becomes ill-defined.

layer2.mapping: Maps volleyball rally events to NFL play sequences where nodes are plays and edges denote temporal order; context augmentation mirrors prior-drive terminal states.
layer2.telemetry: Rally prediction accuracy, set-location classification, hit outcome precision.

primitives.name: Context-Augmented Node Representation
primitives.verbatim_quote: Context augmentation: set prediction supplements the current pass/set nodes with the previous round's hit/block nodes; hit prediction adds the previous round's block node.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'h_{t-1}': 'prior hit node representation', 'b_{t-1}': 'prior block node representation', 'x_t': 'current node features'}
primitives.assumptions: Prior rounds' outcomes influence current prediction; context nodes are additive features.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When prior rounds are missing or mislabeled, context becomes noisy or absent.

layer2.mapping: Extends node embedding space with prior-round representations; enables memory-based inference in GSE's state transition models.
layer2.telemetry: Set prediction accuracy, hit classification F1-score.

primitives.name: Graph Neural Network Architecture
primitives.verbatim_quote: Architectures: - GCN: one graph convolution layer, global pooling, three dense layers.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'W^{(l)}': 'learnable weight matrix at layer l', 'A_{ij}': 'adjacency matrix element indicating edge between i and j', 'H^{(l)}': 'hidden representation at layer l'}
primitives.assumptions: Node features propagate via adjacency matrix; message-passing is linear in node embeddings.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When graph size exceeds memory limits or connectivity is sparse, convergence slows or fails.

layer2.mapping: Applies to NFL drive modeling where plays are nodes; message-passing simulates strategic flow between plays; pooling aggregates drive-level features.
layer2.telemetry: Drive outcome prediction accuracy, Brier score, AUC.

reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight of temporal contact graph encoding lies in representing volleyball rallies as directed graphs where nodes correspond to ball contacts and edges denote sequential dependencies. This formulation allows for structured learning over event sequences rather than flat feature vectors. The graph convolution operation aggregates neighborhood information iteratively, enabling models to learn complex interaction patterns among contacts. Context augmentation enriches this by incorporating prior-round outcomes, which is mathematically modeled as an additional input layer that modifies node embeddings before propagation. The resulting representations are then passed through dense layers for final classification or regression. In GSE, this translates to modeling NFL drives as temporal graphs with plays as nodes and transitions as edges, where prior drive outcomes inform current state predictions. The failure mode arises when contact data is fragmented or mislabeled, leading to disconnected components or incorrect edge structures. Leakage occurs if future events are inadvertently used during training, undermining generalization. Thus, strict temporal ordering and holdout validation are essential.
